name: Planning a Kitchen Island Installation: A Project Timeline

step.name: Step 1: Rough-in planning and clearance verification
step.text: The project team measures your room dimensions to ensure adequate space around the planned footprint. Professional guidelines from the NKBA suggest work aisles of at least 42 inches for single cooks and 48 inches for multiple cooks, with general walkways measuring at least 36 inches. This planning phase typically takes a few days to coordinate layout, verify appliance door swings, and locate subfloor utility access points.

step.name: Step 2: Subfloor utility rough-ins
step.text: If your island includes a sink, dishwasher, microwave drawer, or code-required electrical outlets, trades rough in the plumbing pipes and electrical wiring through the floor. A licensed electrician and plumber handle these lines to meet local building safety requirements before flooring is finished, usually taking 1 to 3 days.

step.name: Step 3: Cabinet assembly and floor anchoring
step.text: Carpenters position the base cabinets, level them meticulously with shims, and screw them into structural cleats fastened directly to the subfloor. Properly anchoring the island prevents movement or tipping under heavy usage, especially once stone tops are added. This carpentry work typically takes 1 day.

step.name: Step 4: Countertop templating and fabrication
step.text: With base cabinets solidly secured and level, the countertop crew takes digital measurements for the worktop. If you have an eating bar with overhangs past 6 to 8 inches, carpenters install concealed steel support brackets directly across the cabinet tops. Fabrication at the shop typically runs between 1 and 3 weeks.

step.name: Step 5: Worktop installation and fixture finish-outs
step.text: Installers deliver and secure the heavy countertop, joining seams cleanly. Finally, trades connect faucets, disposals, cooktops, and outlets, followed by a final inspection of all drawers and trim.
